traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Cyperaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina undivided in all; Britannica says blades mostly linear, flat or folded, never lobed.

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Cyperaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade edges mostly entire but often carrying prickle hairs (a minutely scabrid, forward-toothed edge); Wikipedia Carex notes some broad blades with very sharp edges. Weighted to Carex and Cyperus, the largest genera; at drawing scale the edge reads as entire.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves, at the base or on the stem, are alternate.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves are usually in three ranks, rarely in two or in many.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 410 Cyperaceae: herbs, rarely almost shrubby; leaves in a basal tuft or low on the stem, with a narrow grass-like blade; flowers tiny, each in the axil of a glume, the glumes in two ranks or spiral on small spikes (spikelets); fruit an indehiscent nutlet. The sedges' nutlet is the vocabulary's achene: one seed in a dry fruit that does not open.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cyperaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually a basal rosette, sometimes no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cyperaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often biennial, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 257, family Cyperaceae: leaf venation parallel; read as "parallel".

traits.sexual_system.note: Ingrouille, Diversity and Evolution of Land Plants (1992) p. 186, family Cyperaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite (e.g. Scirpus), sometimes. Ingrouille, Diversity and Evolution of Land Plants (1992) p. 186, family Cyperaceae: sexual system monoecious (e.g. Carex), often. Read together as {"monoecious": "often", "hermaphrodite": "sometimes"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cyperaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded often a rhizome, often tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.stem_cross_section.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 259, 260, 261, family Cyperaceae: stems 3-sided, with solid pith; read as {"trigonous": "usually"}.
